7 ἀποτέλεσε cod. 8 αὐτῷ cod. 16 συγγράψεται cod. 19 ἑαυτῷ coni.
Parmentier. 23 ἐλπίζει vix sanum ; ἐκλείπει coni. Boll : ἐλπίζεις ἐπικράτειαν coni.
Bidez. 27 ἀποστήτων σάντων ut vid. cod. Fort. ἀποστασιασάντων.
sections.en: 7 ἀποτέλεσε ('he completed') the codex has. 8 αὐτῷ ('to him') the codex has. 16 συγγράψεται ('he will write') the codex has. 19 ἑαυτῷ ('to himself') conjectured by Parmentier. 23 ἐλπίζει ('he hopes') scarcely sound; ἐκλείπει ('it fails') conjectured by Boll: ἐλπίζεις ἐπικράτειαν ('you hope for mastery') conjectured by Bidez. 27 ἀποστήτων σάντων ('of those who revolted' - corrupted) as it seems the codex has. Perhaps ἀποστασιασάντων ('of those who revolted').

Araber, p. 7, no 13, p. 10, no 17) aut Jahjâ ben Gâlib discipulum Masallae (cf. ibid.,
p. 9, no 17).
1 Φάδαρ est, ni fallimur, Fadl (Fadal) ben Sachl el Sarachsi, minister (vizir) Cha-
lifae el Mamûn, idemque astrologus, quem Omaris el Tabâri familiarem fuisse
scimus, cf. p. 143, n. 1. Vide Suter, op. cit., p. 7, nos 11 et 13 qui ipse hunc virum
nobis indicavit.
2 Harun al-Rašid.
3 * Cum apostatis verae theologiae „ (fikh = theologia, faḳih = theologus)
[Suter]. Sed potius de Africa loqui videtur Apomasar quae regnante Rašido
defecit; cf. Weil, Gesch. der Khalifen, II, p. 151 ss.
sections.en: Araber, p. 7, no 13, p. 10, no 17) or Jahjâ ben Gâlib, a disciple of Masalla (cf. ibid., p. 9, no 17). 1 Φάδαρ ('Phadar') is, unless we are mistaken, Fadl (Fadal) ben Sachl el Sarachsi, minister (vizier) of Caliph el Mamûn, and the same astrologer whom we know to have been an intimate of Omar el Tabâri, cf. p. 143, n. 1. See Suter, op. cit., p. 7, nos 11 and 13, who himself pointed out this man to us. 2 Harun al-Rašid. 3 * With the apostates of true theology „ (fikh = theology, faḳih = theologian) [Suter]. But rather Apomasar seems to speak about Africa, which revolted while Rašid was reigning; cf. Weil, Gesch. der Khalifen, II, p. 151 ss.

summary.headline: Phadar’s Lunar-Mars Lifespan Method
summary.text: Astrological anecdotes attributed to Phadar and Apomasar: a lunar-Mars method for calculating lifespan, a warning that astrologers should conceal advanced theorems, and a prophecy of the decline of Arab dominion after the reign of Harun al-Rashid.
